I would say this game is slightly above neutral. It's good at what it does, which is an empire manager. It's not anything exceptional, but it's not anything bad. Some of the research paths don't make sense, as you can research and produce flying vehicles without researching flight. The graphics look good, they're just cartoonish/board-game-ish. Long animations (e.g. distant walks) are quite inconvenient, as the game will not let you go to the next turn until an animation is completed. I enjoyed Civ 4 more than this one back when I owned it on disk, but this one is totally fine.

It does work on Linux, but don't use the Linux version of the game. Force the use of a compatibility tool and run the Windows version; it has less issues.

I would say this game is slightly above neutral. It's good at what it does, which is an empire manager. It's not anything exceptional, but it's not anything bad. Some of the research paths don't make sense, as you can research and produce flying vehicles without researching flight. The graphics look good, they're just cartoonish/board-game-ish. Long animations (e.g. distant walks) are quite inconvenient, as the game will not let you go to the next turn until an animation is completed. I enjoyed Civ 4 more than this one back when I owned it on disk, but this one is totally fine.

It does work on Linux, but don't use the Linux version of the game. Force the use of a compatibility tool and run the Windows version; it has less issues.

single_points.text: One reviewer says that almost every opponent AI civ hates you for literally no reason on higher difficulties.

citation.review_text:
It's definitely a major upgrade from Civilization V (especially with the DLCs). In my opinion, it is the most "complete" game of the series, with great game mechanics, hours long sessions, infinite replay-ability etc.
The only con is that AI interactions feel unrealistic against higher difficulty AIs (to be precise, almost every opponent AI civ "hates" you for literally no reason, and they consider that a mechanic to raise difficulty. What I see there is lack of creativity.)

Overall: I highly recommend. Best Civ game and one of the best strategy games.

citations.review_text:
The best strategy game ever.
Perfect for solo strategy gameplay or playing with others, There is a lot of choice when it comes to difficulty, only real bad thing in my opinion is that the harder difficulty AI get a lot richer and stronger but still lack strategy and will struggle to fight.

I've played Civ for most of my life. And while i do enjoy it. The biggest issue is the Ai. The more you play the more you realize that the crappy Ai just takes away from the game so much. Even with mods you really cant correct the underlaying behavior that just ruins the whole experience. After a few hours on a map i always find myself just quitting because after a while you just realize the Ai just isn't doing anything to really challenge you. Mid to late game you just leave them in the dust technologically, and you'll be attacking cities with jets and planes and they are barely in the medieval era. Naval warfare just doesn't exist. You'll mostly just use it to bomb their cities, but they never send anything out to appose your ships whatsoever. I've tried every mod out there, and barely do anything to remedy it, often just making frustrating unexpected behavioral consequences.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features district planning and tiles where wonders and districts are built within a city's borders, alongside unstacked units that can share tiles based on their type.

citations.review_text: ~1700 hoursCiv 6 is still the best version of the series for me. After all these hours it just keeps being fun.You actually have control over your empire. District planning, governors, loyalty, great people, religion, and all the systems reward you for thinking ahead and optimizing. Nothing feels like it’s forcing you down a path or doing the work for you. When something goes wrong, it’s usually because of a decision you made, not the game just deciding something for you.The expansions and all the content give it huge replayability. There are so many different ways to play, and the mod scene is still active if you want even more.I’ve tried Civ 7 for a couple hundred hours and the graphics are nice, but it doesn’t come close to this for me. Civ 6 just feels better to play. Still one of my favorite strategy games.

giant digital board game strategy experience. introduces to the series buildable districts and that these and wonders are now built on tiles in a city's borders. continues from civ 5 that units don't stack but can share tiles with a different type (combat/support/civilian/religious). a bunch of game modes and victory paths and nice polished ui with map pins and various lenses and reports
